transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess the main thing is I just don’t feel like myself anymore. It’s hard to explain without making it sound like I’m just being lazy, but it’s not that. I used to do things. I used to hike a lot, I coached, I played guitar—nothing professional or anything, just something I actually cared about—and I used to call people back when they reached out.

Now I don’t really do any of it. I’ll see a message and just… not answer. Not because I’m mad at them. I just can’t seem to make myself do it. Same with the guitar, it’s sitting there, and I know I could pick it up, but I don’t. Some days I’m in that small rental place for hours, and I know there are things I should be doing—basic things, regular life things—but I just sit there like I can’t get started. It’s like something in me shut off, and I don’t know how to turn it back on.
How long have you been feeling this way—since when did you first notice this shift in yourself?

I think it really started after I moved into the smaller rental place, after the divorce. That was… about a year and two months ago now, I guess. It didn’t happen all at once, or at least I didn’t notice it that way. At first I told myself it was just the move, you know, getting used to being in a different place, smaller space, everything feeling temporary. I figured I’d settle in and get back to normal.

But looking back, that’s when things started unraveling. Little things at first, then more and more. And now it feels like I’ve been sliding for most of that time. So… yeah, about fourteen months, give or take.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like that, no.

I mean, I’ve had times where I stayed up too late, or where I was wired because of stress or because my mind wouldn’t settle, but I wouldn’t call it feeling good or elated. I haven’t had several days where I suddenly felt amazing or like I had all this extra energy and didn’t need sleep. If anything, lately it’s more like I’m dragging myself through the day.

I guess I’m not totally sure where the line is with that kind of thing, but nothing comes to mind where people would’ve said, “You’re acting unusually up,” or where I felt on top of the world for days. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that.
Over these past 14 months, have you felt this way pretty much every day without much change, or have there been stretches where you felt noticeably better or worse than other times?

It’s… it’s been more like an unraveling than a clean up-and-down pattern, if that makes sense. Like, since I moved into that smaller rental after the divorce—so, about a year and two months ago—things just started coming apart little by little.

I wouldn’t say there was some stretch where I was suddenly back to normal and everything felt okay again. Maybe there were individual days where I told myself, “Alright, maybe I’m getting a handle on this,” but when I look at the whole thing, it’s mostly been this long slide. Some weeks feel worse than others, sure, but it all kind of traces back to that move. That’s when I started noticing I wasn’t really bouncing back.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions, or started any new medications, in the time leading up to when these feelings began?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean… I’m trying to go back over it in my head, because the timing all kind of blends together now, but I don’t remember some doctor telling me I had a new medical condition right before all this started.

And medications… I don’t think I started anything new around then either. Nothing that stands out, anyway. I’m not saying my memory of that whole period is perfect, because it was a messy time and I wasn’t exactly keeping careful track of everything, but there wasn’t some obvious new pill or diagnosis where I thought, “Oh, this started after that.”

It felt more tied to everything changing after the move, if anything. But medically, no, I don’t really have something specific to point to.

Before this period started about 14 months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of low mood, low energy, or loss of interest in things that lasted two weeks or more at some earlier point in your life?

I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear memory of another time before this where it was like… two weeks or more of the same kind of low mood or no energy. I mean, I’ve had hard periods in my life, like anyone, where things were stressful or I wasn’t myself for a bit, but I’m having trouble separating that from what you mean clinically.

Before this last year or so, I don’t think I would’ve described myself as being stuck in it for weeks at a time the way I have been now. At least nothing is coming to mind that feels comparable. It’s possible there were shorter times where I felt down, but if you’re asking whether I remember a definite earlier stretch of two weeks or longer like this… I don’t think so. Not that I can point to.
During this past year or so, have you had any thoughts of death or that you'd be better off not being here, or feelings that you're worthless or a burden to others?

I… I don’t think so, not in the way you’re asking. I’ve had plenty of times where I felt worn down or like I didn’t know how I was going to keep dealing with things, but I can’t really say I’ve been sitting there thinking I should be dead or that everyone would be better off without me.

The “worthless” or “burden” part is harder to answer, because I can be pretty harsh on myself, and I’ll think I’m not handling things the way I should. But I don’t know that I’d put it as, like, “I’m worthless.” It’s more… frustration, or disappointment in myself, maybe. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.

So, no, I don’t have a clear thing to tell you there. Not that I’ve noticed in a direct way.

During this past year, have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or ability to concentrate—things like sleeping much more or less than usual, eating significantly more or less, or having real trouble focusing on tasks?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean answer on that. I mean, I know you’re asking about concrete things—sleep, eating, concentration—and I wish I could just say yes or no, but I haven’t really tracked it in a way where I can separate what’s unusual from what’s just… life being off.

Sleep has been kind of variable, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it “much more” or “much less” in a definite way. Some nights are better than others. Appetite, same thing—I haven’t noticed some big change like suddenly not eating or eating constantly. At least not something that stuck out to me as a major symptom.

Concentration is harder, because there are times I feel scattered or like it takes me longer to stay with something, but I don’t know if that’s because of mood, stress, not sleeping well, or just being preoccupied. I can’t honestly say, “Yes, this clearly changed in this specific way.” It’s more like… everything has felt harder to organize, but I don’t have a neat example that proves it.

At its worst during this past year, has your mood and low energy been severe enough to interfere significantly with things like going to work, taking care of yourself, or maintaining relationships—not just feeling 'off,' but genuinely struggling to function?

Yeah… I mean, yes. That part I can answer more clearly, even if it’s hard to talk about.

It got bad enough that it affected work in a serious way. I was doing protective service work, and during what should’ve been a routine patrol, I ended up scaring staff and some bystanders. I don’t like saying it that way, because in my head at the time it didn’t feel like I was trying to scare anyone, but that’s what happened. People were alarmed, and afterward I got suspended from the job. So that’s not just me feeling a little off or having a bad week. That was my functioning falling apart in a place where I’m supposed to be steady and reliable.

And after that, things kind of… narrowed. I pulled back from coaching, and from volunteering, and from people who used to count on me. I used to be someone who showed up for things, you know? If there was a team or a community thing or someone needed help, I was there. But over the past year, especially since the work situation, I’ve just withdrawn more and more. It’s not like I made one big announcement that I was quitting everything. I just stopped answering as much, stopped going, stopped putting myself in positions where people expected me to be dependable.

So yes, it’s interfered. Work, relationships, commitments—pretty much the parts of my life where I used to feel useful.
Over the past year, have you noticed feeling unusually tired or drained of energy nearly every day, even after resting or sleeping?

Yeah… but I’m not sure if I’d describe it exactly like being sleepy all the time. It’s more like I don’t have the drive in me anymore. Like something that used to push me forward just isn’t there.

I used to hike a lot, coach, play guitar, call people back when they reached out—normal things that made me feel like myself. And over this past year, I’ve let almost all of that drop off. It’s not always because I’m lying in bed exhausted, though some days I do feel drained. It’s more like I’ll be sitting in that small rental place for hours, knowing there are things I need to do—laundry, dishes, returning a message, even just getting out for a walk—and I just can’t get myself started. I’ll think, “Okay, get up now,” and then another hour is gone.

Rest doesn’t really fix it. I can sleep or sit quietly and still feel like I’m moving through mud. So yes, I guess I’d say I’ve felt drained a lot, nearly every day in some form, but it’s not just tired. It’s like I don’t feel like myself anymore.

This keeps both persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) and unspecified depressive disorder (F32.9) viable, pending clarification on symptom severity/duration meeting full major depressive episode criteria.

doctor.intent: Assess whether symptoms have been severe enough to significantly impair daily functioning (work, relationships, self-care) at any point, which helps distinguish a full major depressive episode from a milder persistent low-grade depression.
doctor.question: At its worst during this past year, has your mood and low energy been severe enough to interfere significantly with things like going to work, taking care of yourself, or maintaining relationships—not just feeling 'off,' but genuinely struggling to function?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I got suspended from protective service work after I scared staff and bystanders during a routine patrol, and since then I’ve pulled away from coaching, volunteering, and most of the people who used to count on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have significantly interfered with work, self-care, or relationships, which is directly about functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, yes. That part I can answer more clearly, even if it’s hard to talk about.

It got bad enough that it affected work in a serious way. I was doing protective service work, and during what should’ve been a routine patrol, I ended up scaring staff and some bystanders. I don’t like saying it that way, because in my head at the time it didn’t feel like I was trying to scare anyone, but that’s what happened. People were alarmed, and afterward I got suspended from the job. So that’s not just me feeling a little off or having a bad week. That was my functioning falling apart in a place where I’m supposed to be steady and reliable.

And after that, things kind of… narrowed. I pulled back from coaching, and from volunteering, and from people who used to count on me. I used to be someone who showed up for things, you know? If there was a team or a community thing or someone needed help, I was there. But over the past year, especially since the work situation, I’ve just withdrawn more and more. It’s not like I made one big announcement that I was quitting everything. I just stopped answering as much, stopped going, stopped putting myself in positions where people expected me to be dependable.

So yes, it’s interfered. Work, relationships, commitments—pretty much the parts of my life where I used to feel useful.

inference.note: The reported functional impairment (job suspension, withdrawal from coaching/relationships) confirms a clinically significant depressive syndrome, but ambiguity about sleep/appetite/concentration changes still prevents fully meeting criteria for a discrete major depressive episode versus a chronic, lower-grade depressive course; both remain plausible pending further symptom clarification.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has significant, persistent fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day, which is a core symptom needed to confirm a major depressive episode versus a more chronic, lower-grade dysthymic pattern.
doctor.question: Over the past year, have you noticed feeling unusually tired or drained of energy nearly every day, even after resting or sleeping?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about low energy or feeling drained over the past year, which is most closely related to diminished motivation and reduced activity in the Negative_Symptoms profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… but I’m not sure if I’d describe it exactly like being sleepy all the time. It’s more like I don’t have the drive in me anymore. Like something that used to push me forward just isn’t there.

I used to hike a lot, coach, play guitar, call people back when they reached out—normal things that made me feel like myself. And over this past year, I’ve let almost all of that drop off. It’s not always because I’m lying in bed exhausted, though some days I do feel drained. It’s more like I’ll be sitting in that small rental place for hours, knowing there are things I need to do—laundry, dishes, returning a message, even just getting out for a walk—and I just can’t get myself started. I’ll think, “Okay, get up now,” and then another hour is gone.

Rest doesn’t really fix it. I can sleep or sit quietly and still feel like I’m moving through mud. So yes, I guess I’d say I’ve felt drained a lot, nearly every day in some form, but it’s not just tired. It’s like I don’t feel like myself anymore.

inference.note: The severity of functional impairment (job suspension after an alarming incident, complete withdrawal from previously valued relationships/activities) and pervasive daily fatigue/anhedonia are more consistent with a major depressive episode than the milder, less impairing course typical of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), so F34.1 is now ruled out.
